title: "Geometric Structure of the Hypershell"

> [!TLDR]
> A microcanonical energy shell lies between two nearby constant-energy surfaces.

Fig. 3.1 gives a schematic two-dimensional section of the accessible shell.

**Fig. 3.1** Microcanonical hypershell in a schematic coordinate–momentum plane. The shaded region lies between ${\energy{\mathcal H}}={\energy{E}}-{\energy{\delta}}$ and ${\energy{\mathcal H}}={\energy{E}}$. The ensemble density is uniform over this region with respect to phase-space measure.

> [!note] Trajectory clarification
> The source caption says that one ergodic trajectory explores the finite-width shell. In an autonomous isolated system, each trajectory keeps its exact energy and remains on one energy surface inside that shell. The shell represents the ensemble's energy tolerance. Also, a projection of a higher-dimensional uniform distribution need not itself be uniform; the drawing is schematic.

## Physical quantities

| Symbol | Unit | Quantity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${\mechanical{q}}$ | $\unit{m}$ | Position coordinate | A Cartesian position; generalized angles are listed separately. |
| ${\mechanical{p}}$ | $\unit{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ | Translational momentum | The momentum conjugate to a Cartesian position. |
| ${\energy{\mathcal H}}$ | $\unit{J}$ | Hamiltonian | The energy function of the system. |
| ${\energy{E}}$ | $\unit{J}$ | Energy | The system energy; subscripts identify levels or allocated energy contributions. |
| ${\energy{\delta}}$ | $\unit{J}$ | Energy-window width | The small energy interval that defines the shell. |
